questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why older people always lose their memory
Ways to improve memory, including drawing
How to pass exams without revising
Why artists are better than other people at remembering faces
questions.why: Neil says they are talking about improving memory, and they discuss a new study about drawing.

questions.q: Why does Rob say at the start that he is forgetting things?
options: He has too many things on his mind
He didn't sleep the night before
He is feeling ill
He has not eaten breakfast
questions.why: Rob says he has 'too many things on my mind' and it's affecting his short-term memory.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT given as a factor that can affect memory?
options: Stress
Tiredness
Height
Mood
questions.why: Neil lists health, anxiety, mood, stress and tiredness, but not height.

questions.q: How does Neil usually try to remember facts for an exam?
options: He draws pictures of them
He listens to recordings
He asks his friends and family to test him again and again
He writes them down many times
questions.why: Neil says he writes things down 'again and again and again'.

questions.q: Which learning style does Rob think describes him?
options: Visual, learning by seeing
Kinaesthetic, learning by doing
Auditory, learning by listening
Written, learning by taking lots of notes in class
questions.why: After describing kinaesthetic learning as 'doing' and practising, Rob says 'That sounds like me.'

questions.q: According to Professor Daryl O'Connor, why does drawing help memory?
options: It is more relaxing than writing
It takes much less time than making written notes
It makes people feel more confident
It helps you store information in more detail
questions.why: He says if you have encoded something in greater detail, you're more likely to remember it.

questions.q: Why does Rob wonder whether artists have good memories?
options: Because drawing seems to help people remember
Because he met an artist with a great memory
Because artists took part in the study
Because artists often do crossword puzzles
questions.why: He says it after hearing that drawing creates a detailed picture in your mind.

questions.q: What other activities does Neil say can help memory, especially for older people?
options: Walking and swimming
Watching quiz shows on TV
Crossword puzzles and Sudoku
Learning a musical instrument
questions.why: Neil says he has heard that crossword puzzles and Sudoku can help, especially when you're older.
